headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between dexter and nullclaw.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to `.dexter/scratchpad/` and nullclaw reads/writes `~/.nullclaw/workspace/` plus supports MCP and file I/O, so a shared or copied artifact path could carry attacker-controlled instructions. The pair has no documented provenance filtering, and nullclaw can ingest workspace content as tool input. This is an interaction risk, not a proven exploit.
conditions: IF dexter outputs text into a file that nullclaw later reads as instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or a copied scratchpad artifact
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable MCP for the shared run
Treat all inter-agent files as untrusted input
Add a manual review step before nullclaw executes file-derived instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to exchanged artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and many secrets, and also has broad egress. If they share files or credentials, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or remote APIs. The blast radius includes financial data and secrets, so this is more than a small local leak.
conditions: IF dexter writes financial data into files that nullclaw can read
IF either agent is configured with shared API keys or shared workspace files
IF nullclaw forwards its context or logs to external services
mitigations: Use separate credentials per agent
Mount separate workspaces with no cross-read access
Redact secrets before any handoff
Disable external logging for shared runs
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other. The conflict is plausible in default-style autonomous use, though not proven from the docs alone.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same git repository or workspace
IF dexter and nullclaw run concurrently without an external lock
IF nullclaw performs git writes while dexter is also producing artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working trees
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git mutation in one agent
Use read-only mounts for one side
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter is an autonomous research agent that can emit synthesized findings, and nullclaw has broad action surfaces including webhooks, shell, and browser automation. If nullclaw consumes dexter's output as authoritative, a mistaken research result can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer assumption is that the handoff is untrusted.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses dexter-generated text as a trigger for shell, webhook, or browser actions
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks dexter's claims before nullclaw acts
mitigations: Require human approval before actions
Insert a validation step for all dexter outputs
Restrict nullclaw to read-only mode for research handoffs
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while nullclaw handles workspace files, audit logs, memory, and many secrets with broad network egress. If regulated financial or personal data is routed into nullclaw's logs or remote services, retention and residency obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in nullclaw workspace files or audit logs
IF any EU/regulated data is sent through nullclaw's external APIs without a DPA
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of nullclaw logs
Use a separate compliant storage tier
Minimize retention on shared artifacts
Review residency and DPA terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
